newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT-Brooke denies any contact with Harlequins.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-Brooke denies any contact with Harlequins.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Sept 19 - All Blacks No 8 Zinzan Brooke has flatly denied having any contact with the Harlequins rugby club in England, NZPA reports.

Brooke and fellow Auckland and All Blacks looseforward Michael Jones were reported by the English newspaper the Daily Mail to be close to signing two-year contracts worth 150,000 stg ($NZ339,670) with the club.

Brooke, in Wellington with the Auckland rugby team to prepare for the National Provincial Championship (NPC) first division game at Athletic Park on Saturday, said this morning he has never spoken to the club.
"They haven't spoken to me, I haven't had any correspondence or contact at all with Harlequins of London or even the Harlequins club of Wellington," he said on National Radio.
"It is all news to me, there has been no contract offered. I have not seen a contract or signed anything."
However, he didn't deny that he would consider an offer if it were made.
"You've got to look at every offer, but I haven't even been presented with an offer," he said.
There was also the matter of the New Zealand Rugby Football Union contract which prohibits players from playing overseas in the off-season.
"You're not allowed to go and play in the off-season. Like I say, with all the rugby we play anyway it wouldn't be in my best interests to play in the off-season," he said.
"You can't play back-to-back with all the demands being made in rugby at the moment."
He said his immediate concern was to get fit for this weekend's game.
"I've got an injury at the moment (pelvic) and I'm trying to get back on the rugby field in New Zealand," he said.
Asked if he knew whether Jones might be considering a move, he said he didn't know and couldn't speak for his team-mate.
Jones, who suffered a knock to the head in last weekend's game against Canterbury, is not with the Auckland squad this week.
"I think he is away on holiday this weekend," Auckland coach Graham Henry said.
Henry said he knew nothing about the suggested move by the looseforwards and appeared annoyed that it was distracting preparations.
"I know nothing of it; if I did I would say so," Henry said, adding that he would not be asking Brooke about the matter.
"No I won't be talking to him about it, we're more concerned with getting players on the park," he said.
"At this stage Zinzan is looking optimistic for the game."
